intro: Cheile Cibinului is a gorge in Romania's Southern Carpathians, reached along a forest road from the village of Gura Raului. Deep inside it stands the Guardian of Cibin, a silver fir about 500 years old and roughly 42 metres tall, taller than a twelve-storey building. It takes eight men with their arms outstretched to encircle its trunk. Local legend ties it to a shepherd who lost his flock in a storm and to Michael the Brave, who briefly united the Romanian lands around 1600.
meta_description: The Guardian of Cibin, Romania: a silver fir about 500 years old and 42 metres tall, deep in the Cibin gorge. Free, reached by forest trail.
question_meta: Cheile Cibinului's remarkable tree is the Guardian of Cibin, a 500 year old, 42-metre silver fir.
question_answer: The remarkable tree of Cheile Cibinului is the Guardian of Cibin (Paznicul Cibinului), a silver fir deep in the gorge, about 12 kilometres up a forest road from Gura Raului village.
question_context: It takes eight men with their arms outstretched to get round this fir, according to a Sibiu newspaper, and at about 42 metres it is taller than a twelve-storey building. Its name comes from a shepherd's legend: caught in a storm, a shepherd sheltered his flock under the fir, and when the storm passed the sheep were gone; he wept and prayed, the tree grew until it was tall enough, and he climbed it and saw his flock grazing in a distant meadow, and it has been the watchman of the gorge since. Every source puts it at about 500 years old, and local lore links it to Michael the Brave, who briefly united the Romanian lands around 1600, though nobody has counted the rings. The trunk is about two metres across at its widest, which works out to roughly six metres round by arithmetic rather than a tape measurement. Two Sibiu papers wrote about the tourists it still draws as recently as September 2024. A marked trail and safety railings lead to it through public forest managed by the Gura Raului forestry district, and the pin is approximate, so follow the trail rather than the dot.

faq.q: What is the remarkable tree in Cheile Cibinului?
faq.a: The Guardian of Cibin (Paznicul Cibinului), a silver fir about 42 metres tall, deep in the gorge on a forest road from Gura Raului.

faq.q: How old is the Guardian of Cibin?
faq.a: About 500 years by every source, though nobody has counted its rings. Local lore ties it to Michael the Brave, around 1600.

faq.q: Can you visit the Guardian of Cibin?
faq.a: Yes, free, no ticket. A marked trail with safety railings leads to it through public forest managed by the Gura Raului forestry district.

faq.q: How do you get to the Guardian of Cibin?
faq.a: No public transport reaches it. By car to Gura Raului village south of Sibiu, then about 12 kilometres along a forest road, finishing on foot on the marked trail.

trees.story:
It takes eight men with their arms outstretched to get round this fir, according to a Sibiu newspaper, and at about 42 metres it is taller than a twelve-storey building. The Guardian of Cibin stands deep in the Cibin gorge in Romania's Southern Carpathians, some twelve kilometres up a forest road from the village of Gura Raului.

Its name comes from a shepherd's legend. Caught in a storm, a shepherd sheltered his flock under the fir, and when the storm passed the sheep were gone. He wept and prayed, the tree grew until it was tall enough, and he climbed it and saw his flock grazing in a distant meadow. Since then it has been the watchman of the gorge.

Every source puts it at about 500 years old. Local lore says it came up in the time of Mihai Viteazul, Michael the Brave, who briefly united the Romanian lands around 1600; the story fits the figure, though nobody has counted the rings. The trunk is about two metres across at its widest, which works out to roughly six metres round; that girth is our arithmetic from the diameter, not a tape measurement.

It is very much alive: two Sibiu papers wrote in September 2024 about the tourists it still draws. A marked trail and safety railings lead to it through public forest managed by the Gura Raului forestry district. The pin is approximate, so follow the trail rather than the dot.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, about 42 metres, and a trunk some two metres across. It stands beside the marked trail with safety railings in the Cibin gorge, about twelve kilometres up the forest road from Gura Raului.
trees.access: Free, no ticket. Stands beside a forest road/marked hiking trail with safety railings inside the Cheile Cibinului gorge, part of a signposted regional trail network (connecting toward Paltinis and Saua Canaia); managed by the Gura Raului forestry district (Ocolul Silvic Gura Raului). Genuinely open public forest land, not private.
trees.transport: No public transport. Reached by car to Gura Raului village (Marginimea Sibiului, south of Sibiu city), then about 12km along a forest road into the Cibin gorge, on foot for the final stretch on the marked trail.
